gnome: 1. An imaginary being, supposed by the Rosicrucians to inhabit the inner parts of the earth, and to be the guardian of mines, quarries, etc. 2. A dwarf; a goblin; a person of small stature or misshapen features, or of strange appearance. 3. (Zoöl.) A small owl (Glaucidium gnoma) of the Western United States. 4. Etym: [Gr. A brief reflection or maxim. Peacham.
gnathostoma: A comprehensive division of vertebrates, including all that have distinct jaws, in contrast with the leptocardians and marsipobranchs (Cyclostoma), which lack them. [Written also Gnathostomata.]
gnathic: Of or pertaining to the jaw. Gnathic index, in a skull, the ratio of the distance from the middle of the nasofrontal suture to the basion (taken equal to 100), to the distance from the basion to the middle of the front edge of the upper jaw; -- called also alveolar index.
gnu: One of two species of large South African antelopes of the genus Catoblephas, having a mane and bushy tail, and curved horns in both sexes. [Written also gnoo.] Note: The common gnu or wildebeest (Catoblephas gnu) is plain brown; the brindled gnu or blue wildebeest (C. gorgon) is larger, with transverse stripes of black on the neck and shoulders.
gnatworm: The aquatic larva of a gnat; -- called also, colloquially, wiggler.
gnomically: In a gnomic, didactic, or sententious manner.
gnathidium: The ramus of the lower jaw of a bird as far as it is naked; -- commonly used in the plural.
gnathopod: A gnathopodite or maxilliped. See Maxilliped.
gnarled: Knotty; full of knots or gnarls; twisted; crossgrained. The unwedgeable and gnarléd oak. Shak.
gnathostegite: One of a pair of broad plates, developed from the outer maxillipeds of crabs, and forming a cover for the other mouth organs.
gnash: To strike together, as in anger or pain; as, to gnash the teeth. | To grind or strike the teeth together. There they him laid, Gnashing for anguish, and despite, and shame. Milton.
gnomologic: Pertaining to, of the nature of, or resembling, a gnomology.
gnathopodite: Any leglike appendage of a crustacean, when modified wholly, or in part, to serve as a jaw, esp. one of the maxillipeds.
gnomic: Sententious; uttering or containing maxims, or striking detached thoughts; aphoristic. A city long famous as the seat of elegiac and gnomic poetry. G. R. Lewes. Gnomic Poets, Greek poets, as Theognis and Solon, of the sixth century B. C., whose writings consist of short sententious precepts and reflections.
gnomonical: Of or pertaining to the gnomon, or the art of dialing. Gnomonic projection, a projection of the circles of the sphere, in which the point of sight is taken at the center of the sphere, and the principal plane is tangent to the surface of the sphere.
gnaw: 1. To bite, as something hard or tough, which is not readily separated or crushed; to bite off little by little, with effort; to wear or eat away by scraping or continuous biting with the teeth; | To use the teeth in biting; to bite with repeated effort, as in eating or removing with the teethsomething hard, unwiedly, or unmanageable. I might well, like the spaniel, gnaw upon the chain that…
gnathite: Any one of the mouth appendages of the Arthropoda. They are known as mandibles, maxillæ, and maxillipeds.
gnawer: 1. One who, or that which, gnaws. 2. (Zoöl.) A rodent.
gnomonics: The art or science of dialing, or of constructing dials to show the hour of the day by the shadow of a gnomon.
gnomical: Sententious; uttering or containing maxims, or striking detached thoughts; aphoristic. A city long famous as the seat of elegiac and gnomic poetry. G. R. Lewes. Gnomic Poets, Greek poets, as Theognis and Solon, of the sixth century B. C., whose writings consist of short sententious precepts and reflections.
gnosticism: The system of philosophy taught by the Gnostics.
gnathotheca: The horney covering of the lower mandible of a bird.
gnarl: To growl; to snarl. And wolves are gnarling who shall gnaw thee first. Shak. | a knot in wood; a large or hard knot, or a protuberance with twisted grain, on a tree.
gnomonically: According to the principles of the gnomonic projection.
gnomonic: Of or pertaining to the gnomon, or the art of dialing. Gnomonic projection, a projection of the circles of the sphere, in which the point of sight is taken at the center of the sphere, and the principal plane is tangent to the surface of the sphere.
gnostic: 1. Knowing; wise; shrewd. [Old Slang] I said you were a gnostic fellow. Sir W. Scott. 2. (Eccl. Hist.) Of or pertaining to Gnosticism or its adherents; as, the Gnostic heresy. | One of the so-called philosophers in the first ages of Christianity, who claimed a true philosophical interpretation of the Christian religion. Their system combined Oriental theology and Greek…
gnoscopine: An alkaloid existing in small quantities in opium.
gneissoid: Resembling gneiss; having some of the characteristics of gneiss; -- applied to rocks of an intermediate character between granite and gneiss, or mica slate and gneiss.
gnarly: Full of knots; knotty; twisted; crossgrained.
gnomology: A collection of, or a treatise on, maxims, grave sentences, or reflections. (old) Milton.
gnar: A knot or gnarl in wood; hence, a tough, thickset man; -- written also gnarr. (old) He was . . . a thick gnarre. Chaucer. | To gnarl; to snarl; to growl; -- written also gnarr. (old) At them he gan to rear his bristles strong, And felly gnarre. Spenser. A thousand wants Gnarr at the heels of men. Tennison.
gnat: 1. (Zoöl.) A blood-sucking dipterous fly, of the genus Culex, undergoing a metamorphosis in water. The females have a proboscis armed with needlelike organs for penetrating the skin of animals. These are wanting in the males. In America they are generally called mosquitoes. See Mosquito. 2. Any fly resembling a Culex in form or habits;
gneissic: Relating to, or resembling, gneiss; consisting of gneiss.
gnide: To rub; to bruise; to break in pieces. (old) Note: This word is found in Tyrwhitt's Chaucer, but improperly. The woed, though common in Old English, does not occur in Chaucer. T. R. Lounsbury.
gnosis: The deeper wisdom; knowledge of spiritual truth, such as was claimed by the Gnostics.
gnomological: Pertaining to, of the nature of, or resembling, a gnomology.
gneiss: A crystalline rock, consisting, like granite, of quartz, feldspar, and mica, but having these materials, especially the mica, arranged in planes, so that it breaks rather easily into coarse slabs or flags. Hornblende sometimes takes the place of the mica, and it is then called hornblendic or syenitic gneiss. Similar varieties of related rocks are also called gneiss.
gnaphalium: A genus of composite plants with white or colored dry and persistent involucres; a kind of everlasting.
gnomon: 1. (Dialing) The style or pin, which by its shadow, shows the hour of the day. It is usually set parallel to the earth's axis. 2. (Astron.) A style or column erected perpendicularly to the horizon, formerly used in astronomocal observations. Its principal use was to find the altitude of the sun by measuring the length of its shadow. 3.
